stories.title: What the Q2 mock budget datasets are doing
stories.dek: A teaching page for the two synthetic zero-based-budgeting datasets built on 13 November 2026: how the generator works, what is in each file, the planted answer key for Q2, the public sources, and the self-checks. Modeled on published totals for Corning and Morgan Stanley. Not either firm's actual budget.

stories.title: Methods scout questions: new Q1 and Q3, old prime-broker Q1 retired
stories.dek: Jared approved two data-supported questions on 14 November 2026. New Q1 asks how Form PF aggregate prime-broker borrowings connect to OFR repo and NY Fed settlement fails. New Q3 asks how supervisory stress-test projections connect to realized Y-9C payouts. The 2026-11-10 prime-broker top-25 share question is retired; only open and in-progress questions are scout targets. Q2 is unchanged.

stories.title: Methods scout, 13 November: ebnm shrinkage and DenseLines charts on synthetic mock budgets (Q2)
stories.dek: The first Q2 run, on clearly labelled SYNTHETIC mock ZBB datasets. ebnm pooling cuts each program's 2025-level error by 21–26%. DenseLines can show a thousand short start-and-stop series once made gap-safe. ebnm is recommended for the promote workflow; DenseLines is interesting.

stories.title: CQL: what the mathematics can compute, and what it cannot
stories.dek: Conexus’s core is a language in which database schemas are equational theories, migrations are adjoint functors, and a theorem prover refuses programs that would break stated constraints. A technical capability review — guarantees, limits, scale — and a comparison with Google Pregel, data-exchange chase engines, and closer Google systems.

stories.title: Scheduled scout (catch-up): ecotraj share trajectories and lphom transfer matrices, aimed at dealer-share dynamics
stories.dek: Ecological trajectory analysis and linear-programming voter-transfer matrices, run on the FR Y-9C trading panel. Residual trading-asset increments are directional; a quarterly flow matrix from this single panel is not identified. ecotraj is recommended for the promote workflow; lphom is interesting.

stories.title: Ad hoc scout: ecological rank clocks and genomic proportionality, aimed at dealer-share dynamics
stories.dek: codyn rank clocks and Lovell proportionality, run on the FR Y-9C trading panel. US dealer volumes co-move; a JPM–GS proportionality signal strengthens after the market is removed. Both methods are recommended for the promote workflow.

stories.title: Secret-sauce plans for changeforest, partykit, MARSS and InspectChangepoint
stories.dek: Exactly three avenues per method — Engineering, Math, and a new use on our data. Plans only; nothing is being built. Later editions the same day append codyn, Lovell proportionality, ecotraj and lphom.

stories.title: Methods scout, 11 November: MARSS and InspectChangepoint on dealer-share dynamics
stories.dek: Aimed at Q1 (market-driven versus sticky dealer shares). A state-space decomposition and a sparse-projection change-point method, each run on the lab’s data.

stories.title: Methods scout, 10 November: partykit trees and changeforest
stories.dek: Conditional-inference and model-based trees from partykit, and random-forest change-point detection from changeforest, each run at least three ways on Drive data.

stories.title: Methods scout: lesser-known methods, run on our data
stories.dek: The daily editions, newest first, plus secret-sauce plans and the watchlist. Each method is run at least three ways on the lab’s own panels.

stories.title: traceot: glass-box optimal-transport regression
stories.dek: A faithful ADOPT (Song & Müller, AISTATS 2026) reproduction, building toward TRACE — splitting a change in distribution shape into composition and response. Rust core and Python. Research, unvalidated. The Pages site holds the v5.1 working paper, gates and learning notes.

stories.title: Optimal transport on kernels: a learning guide
stories.dek: Markov–Wasserstein kernels, Bayesian inference, augmented encoders, and the MaWa and WaCo losses. A long-form lab learning page.

stories.title: Optimal transport for operations research, risk and planning: classical methods
stories.dek: Sourced notes on classical statistics and machine-learning methods built on Wasserstein spaces, including a small-N toolkit for N < 100.

stories.title: BankGraph: our own relational benchmark, from the Drive data
stories.dek: A specification, scripts and validation baselines for a relational benchmark the lab built itself, rather than borrowing a generic graph-ML toy set.

stories.title: KumoRFM on NVIDIA NIM: a learning note and an honest test
stories.dek: What Kumo’s relational foundation model is, how the NIM endpoint is supposed to work, and a frank account of testing it.

stories.title: CFPB complaints × OT: killed at burn-in (negative result)
stories.dek: Burn-in median next-month W₂² of 0.0064 was below the half-sample noise floor of 0.0269: month-to-month change in the cross-company shape of complaints is below sampling noise. The pre-registered rule killed the object. No out-of-sample run.

stories.title: CFPB complaints: what the forecast was going to test
stories.dek: A learning page on forecasting the shape of complaints, not a single company’s total — and why the study stopped at the gate.

stories.title: FDIC branch deposits × OT: killed at burn-in (negative result)
stories.dek: Next-year change in the within-state spread of branch deposits was below the half-sample noise floor in all nine burn-in years (median W₂² 0.0078 versus 0.0196); planning power 0.07 with 22 test years. No out-of-sample run.

stories.title: FDIC branch deposits: what the forecast was going to test
stories.dek: Forecasting the shape of a state’s bank branches, and why the study stopped at the burn-in gate.

stories.title: Analysis skills: a methods newsroom
stories.dek: General agent analysis skills, in Claude Code format, promoted from scouted methods through a reproduce-then-promote workflow. The Pages site is a newsroom of promoted skills and method articles, with links back to the lab’s scout editions.

stories.title: Nitro XML: Office files, read and viewed in the browser
stories.dek: A Rust and WebAssembly port of the read/view path of ChristopherVR/ooxml — Word, Excel and PowerPoint — rendered fully in the browser. The site has the plan and a live demo.

stories.title: Nitro XML: live demos
stories.dek: Open .docx, .xlsx and .pptx files in the browser, full-page or embedded, from the Nitro XML Pages site.

stories.title: Jev Ultrafast research-browser eval harness
stories.dek: A reproducible evaluation harness and field note for Jev Ultrafast: QC’d cases, stress suites, a suite runner and a report generator. Public repository; no GitHub Pages site. Not investment advice.

stories.title: Financial statement forecasting on the FR Y-9C panel
stories.dek: Non-embedding methods for joint multi-item forecasting of bank holding-company income statements and balance sheets — empirical-Bayes panels, chained GBM, MIDAS, MinT reconciliation. FR Y-9C with a Yahoo Finance smoke path.

stories.title: Teaching: non-embedding forecasting of financial statements
stories.dek: A teaching note on the statement-forecast track: the problem, the methods, and how they sit on the FR Y-9C panel.

stories.title: Lit memo: non-embedding financial-statement forecasting
stories.dek: A literature map for fundamentals forecasting without embeddings, aimed at the FR Y-9C BHC panel.

stories.title: Results: empirical-Bayes statement forecasts
stories.dek: Pre-registered empirical-Bayes forecasts of three quarterly Y-9C income-statement lines, with walk-forward errors and Diebold–Mariano tests.

stories.title: Teaching: naive / pooled-AR forecast combination
stories.dek: A walk-forward combination of the naive and pooled growth-AR forecasts, with one pooled weight per line, on the top-50 Y-9C filers.

stories.title: Results: naive / pooled-AR forecast combination
stories.dek: Pre-registered walk-forward combination of naive and pooled-AR forecasts of three quarterly Y-9C income-statement lines.

stories.title: Y-9C and Yahoo bank quarterly panels
stories.dek: The research data path for bank-statement forecasting: FFIEC NIC FR Y-9C bulk downloads and Yahoo Finance quarterly smoke. Panel assembly, alignment notes, and known quirks.

stories.title: Results: next-quarter net interest income
stories.dek: Reproducible next-quarter NII forecasts for the largest 50 Y-9C filers at each origin.

stories.title: Y-9C trading revenue × optimal transport
stories.dek: Pre-registered forecasts of FR Y-9C trading revenue (BHCKA220): per-bank baselines with W₂-barycenter combination and Wasserstein autoregression of the cross-section.

stories.title: Results: Y-9C trading revenue — primary FAIL, run incomplete
stories.dek: One authorized out-of-sample run: primary FAIL on both hypotheses; the run stopped in a sensitivity. Baselines plus optimal-transport layers, as pre-registered.

stories.title: DFM × Sinkhorn nowcasting
stories.dek: Literature at the intersection of dynamic factor models (ragged-edge nowcasting) and Sinkhorn / entropic optimal transport as an observation or imputation loss. A thin but real intersection, anchored by Spelta et al. (JRSS-A 2025).

stories.title: Teaching: dynamic-factor nowcasting meets Sinkhorn loss
stories.dek: Why the intersection is interesting, what the literature actually contains, and a research recipe.

stories.title: Lit memo: DFM forecasting ∩ Sinkhorn-as-loss
stories.dek: Cluster map, the true intersection, adjacent papers, and open questions.

stories.title: Lab plan: CP funding forecasts (9 October 2026)
stories.dek: Which forecasts of commercial-paper issuance and maturity mix are best, whether any helps spot funding stress early, and whether optimal transport earns a place against strong baselines.

stories.title: Fed CP maturity mix × OT: passed burn-in, awaiting approval
stories.dek: Pre-registration and hashes for an applied lab study of commercial-paper issuance maturity mix, with OT as one candidate. Passed burn-in, pinned. Nothing held out has been scored.

stories.title: Commercial-paper maturity mix: what the burn-in gate found
stories.dek: The short learning page for the Fed CP study’s burn-in result.

stories.title: Fed CP OT: what PREREG v2 pins, and why
stories.dek: An explainer for the v2 pre-registration, which resolved a review of the first pin. Out-of-sample work is not authorised by this page.

stories.title: Commercial-paper maturity mix: app placeholder
stories.dek: A placeholder page for a Fed CP maturity-mix application. The pre-registration and learning pages are the substantive documents.

stories.title: USA ETF Lab: a transparent feature-and-scoring pipeline
stories.dek: Feature extraction and scoring for a pre-approved USA ETF research universe, with optional thematic rotation and walk-forward research artifacts. A separate GitHub Pages site — the work the lab home used to mention without a link. Research only; not investment advice.

stories.title: ECM Momentum Graph: equity-issuance economics from SEC filings
stories.dek: A pipeline over SEC EDGAR prospectus filings that extracts deal economics, underwriters and metadata, with evidence tracking, for ECM volume and revenue potential. Public repository; no Pages site.

stories.title: M&A Financing Graph: deals and debt underwriting from EDGAR
stories.dek: Ingests SEC filings and extracts M&A parties, advisory banks, debt-financing events and underwriting syndicates, with modeled revenue attribution and source citations. Public repository; no Pages site.

stories.title: Financing Private Credit: a NY Fed SR 1111 reproduction, extended
stories.dek: A modular indicator framework that began as a reproduction of New York Fed Staff Report 1111 and now supports broader credit and financing indicators, including nowcasting and Monte Carlo forecasts. Public repository; no Pages site.

stories.title: Causal Conditional Flow Matching
stories.dek: A generative time-series framework based on continuous normalising flows with causal-structure enforcement. Public repository; no Pages site.

stories.title: Meistar-KG: papers into personalised audio learning sessions
stories.dek: An agentic architecture that turns a paper URL into a Feynman-style lecture, with a personal knowledge graph, TTS playback and a live Q&A agent. Public repository; no Pages site.

stories.title: Gridley Excavating
stories.dek: The website for Gridley Excavating, LLC — gravel, topsoil and mulch in Corning, NY. A GitHub Pages site on a custom domain, included so every Pages property under this account is reachable from this home.
